```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Abdallah_2017_tocilizumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Abdallah_2017_tocilizumab"))$description`
* Article: [J Clin Pharmacol. 2017;57(4):459-468](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.826)
  (open access, PMC5363244). The supporting information holds the baseline
  demographics (Table S1), the PK-substudy NCA (Tables S2 and S3) and
  goodness-of-fit plots; it holds no model code and no variance estimates.

# Population

Abdallah 2017 pooled the 24-week double-blind periods of two phase 3 trials in
adults with moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis and an inadequate response
to DMARDs, all on stable background non-biologic DMARDs:

* **SUMMACTA** (NCT01194414): tocilizumab 162 mg SC every week (QW) versus
  8 mg/kg IV every 4 weeks (Q4W; flat 800 mg for patients weighing >= 100 kg).
* **BREVACTA** (NCT01232569): tocilizumab 162 mg SC every 2 weeks (Q2W) versus
  placebo.

The population PK dataset had 1759 patients and 13 642 serum samples, mostly
predose, with intensive sampling in PK substudies. In the safety populations
(Supplementary Table S1) about 83% were female, mean age was 52-53 years and
mean body weight was 70.3-74.6 kg (SD 16.6-19.1 kg) by arm; 23-27% weighed
less than 60 kg and 6-10% weighed 100 kg or more. The Results describe 40 and
140 kg as close to the extremes of weight in the study population.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Abdallah_2017_tocilizumab")$population`.

# Source trace

The final model is a two-compartment model with first-order SC absorption, SC
bioavailability and parallel linear and Michaelis-Menten elimination from the
central compartment (Results, Pharmacokinetics; Discussion). Body weight was
the only strong covariate.

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 2-compartment, first-order SC absorption, linear + Michaelis-Menten elimination | -- | Abstract; Results 'Pharmacokinetics'; Discussion |
| CL (L/day) | 0.216 (216 mL/day) | Table 1A, theta1 |
| V2, central volume (L) | 4.5 | Table 1A, theta2 |
| Q (L/day) | 0.274 (274 mL/day) | Table 1A, theta3 |
| V3, peripheral volume (L) | 2.8 | Table 1A, theta4 |
| VM (mg/L/day) | 1.9 | Table 1A, theta5 |
| KM (ug/mL) | 0.34 | Table 1A, theta6 |
| ka (1/day) | 0.23 | Table 1A, theta7 |
| FSC (fraction) | 0.795 | Results text '79.5%' (Table 1A rounds to 0.80) |
| Weight exponent on CL and Q | 0.51 | Results, 'Effect of Body Weight ...' |
| Weight exponent on V2 and V3 | 0.68 | Results, 'Effect of Body Weight ...' |
| Reference weight | 70 kg | Results, 'CL ~ (WT/70)^CLWT' |
| IIV, residual error | not reported | -- |

# Virtual cohort

The model carries no inter-individual variability, so the only between-subject
difference is body weight. Weight is taken as a deterministic grid: 200
equally spaced quantiles of a log-normal distribution with mean 73 kg and SD
18.5 kg (the pooled Table S1 values), restricted to the 40-150 kg range by
spacing the quantiles inside that range rather than clamping. The same weight
grid is used for all three regimens. The grid reproduces the Table S1 weight
bands (about 25% below 60 kg and 8% at or above 100 kg).

```{r cohort}
n_per_arm <- 200
wt_mean <- 73
wt_sd <- 18.5
sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (wt_sd / wt_mean)^2))
meanlog <- log(wt_mean) - sdlog^2 / 2
p_lo <- plnorm(40, meanlog, sdlog)
p_hi <- plnorm(150, meanlog, sdlog)
p <- p_lo + (seq_len(n_per_arm) - 0.5) / n_per_arm * (p_hi - p_lo)
wt_grid <- qlnorm(p, meanlog, sdlog)

wt_band <- function(wt) {
  cut(wt, c(-Inf, 60, 100, Inf), right = FALSE,
      labels = c("<60 kg", "60 to <100 kg", ">=100 kg"))
}
knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(table(wt_band(wt_grid))) |>
    mutate(pct = round(100 * Freq / n_per_arm, 1)) |>
    rename("Weight band" = Var1, "n" = Freq, "%" = pct),
  caption = "Weight-band composition of the virtual cohort."
)
```

# Simulation

Each regimen is dosed for 24 weeks (to day 168), as in the double-blind
periods. The IV dose is 8 mg/kg, capped at a flat 800 mg for patients weighing
100 kg or more, given as a 1-hour infusion.

```{r simulate}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Abdallah_2017_tocilizumab"))

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,       ~route, ~tau,
  "162 mg SC QW",   "SC",   7,
  "162 mg SC Q2W",  "SC",   14,
  "8 mg/kg IV Q4W", "IV",   28
)

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 168, by = 0.25),
  seq(0, 1, by = 1 / 48),
  140 + seq(0, 1, by = 1 / 48)
)))

make_arm <- function(i) {
  a <- arms[i, ]
  dose_times <- seq(0, 168 - a$tau, by = a$tau)
  id <- (i - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  subj <- tibble(id = id, WT = wt_grid)
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(
      evid = 1L,
      cmt = if (a$route == "SC") "depot" else "central",
      amt = if (a$route == "SC") 162 else ifelse(WT >= 100, 800, 8 * WT),
      dur = if (a$route == "SC") 0 else 1 / 24
    )
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0, dur = 0)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(treatment = a$treatment) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), make_arm))
# rate is only meaningful for the IV infusion; SC doses are boluses into depot.
events <- events |>
  mutate(rate = ifelse(evid == 1 & dur > 0, amt / dur, 0)) |>
  select(-dur)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = c("treatment", "WT"),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
sim <- sim |> mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = arms$treatment))
```

## Steady-state profiles (Figure 2)

```{r fig2, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Abdallah 2017: cohort-mean tocilizumab concentration over weeks 20-24 for each regimen."}
fig2 <- sim |>
  filter(time >= 140, time <= 168) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(Cc = mean(Cc), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(fig2, aes(time / 7, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("blue", "darkgreen", "black")) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Tocilizumab concentration (ug/mL)", colour = NULL)
```

Figure 2 of the paper shows an IV peak of about 150 ug/mL at week 20 falling
to about 17 ug/mL at week 24, an SC QW profile oscillating between about 42
and 48 ug/mL, and an SC Q2W profile between about 3 and 10 ug/mL.
The simulated cohort means are close for the SC QW and IV regimens; the SC
Q2W trough is lower, for the reason discussed under Table 2 below.

## Week-24 trough by weight band (Table 2)

```{r table2}
trough_wk24 <- sim |>
  filter(abs(time - 168) < 1e-6) |>
  mutate(band = wt_band(WT)) |>
  group_by(treatment, band) |>
  summarise(sim_median = median(Cc), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

published_t2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,       ~band,           ~pub_median,
  "162 mg SC QW",   "<60 kg",        59.8,
  "162 mg SC QW",   "60 to <100 kg", 40.5,
  "162 mg SC QW",   ">=100 kg",      19.7,
  "162 mg SC Q2W",  "<60 kg",        10.6,
  "162 mg SC Q2W",  "60 to <100 kg", 2.6,
  "162 mg SC Q2W",  ">=100 kg",      0.2,
  "8 mg/kg IV Q4W", "<60 kg",        10.6,
  "8 mg/kg IV Q4W", "60 to <100 kg", 16.4,
  "8 mg/kg IV Q4W", ">=100 kg",      24.3
)
t2 <- trough_wk24 |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment), band = as.character(band)) |>
  left_join(published_t2, by = c("treatment", "band")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_median - pub_median) / pub_median)

t2 |>
  mutate(sim_median = signif(sim_median, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = treatment, "Weight band" = band, "n (sim)" = n,
    "Simulated median Ctrough (ug/mL)" = sim_median,
    "Published model-predicted median (ug/mL)" = pub_median,
    "% difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median steady-state trough by baseline weight band: simulated vs Table 2 of Abdallah 2017 (model-predicted).")
```

The SC QW and IV Q4W medians agree with the published model predictions. The
SC Q2W medians do not, and the gap is expected: at Q2W the trough falls into
the range of KM (0.34 ug/mL), where the Michaelis-Menten pathway makes the
trough very sensitive to each subject's clearance and volume. The published
values come from simulations with inter-individual variability, which this
typical-value model cannot reproduce because the variance estimates were not
reported. The checks below therefore assert only on the QW and IV arms.

```{r table2-check}
chk_t2 <- t2 |> filter(treatment != "162 mg SC Q2W")
stopifnot(
  # The QW regimen is far above KM, so its trough is set by the linear
  # clearance and the weight exponents; a mis-transcribed CL, F, V or exponent
  # moves these medians by tens of percent.
  all(abs(chk_t2$pct_diff[chk_t2$treatment == "162 mg SC QW"]) < 20),
  # IV troughs are smaller and closer to the nonlinear range; allow 30%.
  all(abs(chk_t2$pct_diff[chk_t2$treatment == "8 mg/kg IV Q4W"]) < 30)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA over the first dosing interval and over the week-20 dosing interval (the
paper's steady state), by regimen.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

tau_tbl <- arms |> select(treatment, tau)
intervals <- bind_rows(
  tau_tbl |> mutate(start = 0, end = tau, interval = "First dosing interval"),
  tau_tbl |> mutate(start = 140, end = 140 + tau, interval = "Steady state (week 20)")
) |>
  mutate(cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE) |>
  select(-tau)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj, dose_obj,
  intervals = as.data.frame(select(intervals, -interval))
))

nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  left_join(intervals |> select(treatment, start, interval),
            by = c("treatment", "start"))
# The trough is the concentration at the end of each interval, read from the
# simulation (PKNCA's ctrough matches `end` against interval-relative times and
# returns NA for an interval that does not start at time 0).
trough <- intervals |>
  select(treatment, interval, end) |>
  left_join(conc_df, by = "treatment", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(abs(time - end) < 1e-6) |>
  transmute(treatment, interval, PPTESTCD = "ctrough", PPORRES = Cc)
nca_mean <- nca_res |>
  select(treatment, interval, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  bind_rows(trough) |>
  group_by(treatment, interval, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(value = mean(PPORRES), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(nca_mean$n == n_per_arm))
```

## Comparison against the published secondary parameters (Table 1B)

Table 1B reports mean values from a 5000-subject simulation that included
inter-individual variability; AUC is converted from ug*h/mL to ug*day/mL.

```{r nca-compare}
published_t1b <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,       ~interval,                 ~cmax, ~ctrough, ~auclast,
  "162 mg SC QW",   "First dosing interval",   9.3,   7.0,   1243 / 24,
  "162 mg SC QW",   "Steady state (week 20)",  51.3,  45.3,  8254 / 24,
  "162 mg SC Q2W",  "First dosing interval",   5.8,   1.0,   1210 / 24,
  "162 mg SC Q2W",  "Steady state (week 20)",  13,    5.9,   3460 / 24,
  "8 mg/kg IV Q4W", "First dosing interval",   136,   7.7,   28824 / 24,
  "8 mg/kg IV Q4W", "Steady state (week 20)",  154,   18.7,  39216 / 24
) |>
  mutate(group = paste(treatment, "-", interval))

sim_wide <- nca_mean |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "ctrough", "auclast")) |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(group = paste(treatment, "-", interval)) |>
  select(group, cmax, ctrough, auclast)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_wide,
  reference = published_t1b |> select(group, cmax, ctrough, auclast),
  by = "group",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", ctrough = "ug/mL", auclast = "ug*day/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Cohort-mean NCA of the simulated cohort vs the mean secondary parameters of Abdallah 2017 Table 1B. Ctrough is the concentration at the end of the dosing interval. * marks rows differing by >20%.")
```

The SC QW and IV Q4W Cmax and AUC agree with Table 1B within 14% in both
intervals, as do the SC QW troughs. The IV first-interval trough (-25%) and
the SC Q2W troughs (about -67%) are lower than published, for the reason given
under Table 2: when concentrations approach KM, a typical-value solve of a
Michaelis-Menten model underpredicts the mean concentration of a population
with variability.

The first-interval SC Q2W column of Table 1B cannot be matched by a model in
which both SC arms receive the same first dose. After the same first 162 mg SC
dose, its AUC over 14 days (1210 ug*h/mL) is smaller than the SC QW AUC over
7 days (1243 ug*h/mL), and its Cmax (5.8 ug/mL) is lower than the SC QW Cmax
(9.3 ug/mL). The two columns must therefore describe differently composed
populations; the Methods compute secondary parameters from each patient's
Bayesian post hoc estimates, while the table footnote describes a 5000-subject
simulation. In the simulation here the first SC dose is identical in the two
SC arms by construction, so the Q2W first-interval Cmax and AUC are flagged.

```{r nca-check}
# Cmax and AUC of the QW and IV regimens, both intervals. These sit well above
# KM, where the typical-value solve and the population mean nearly coincide.
ss <- nca_mean |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast"), treatment != "162 mg SC Q2W") |>
  left_join(
    published_t1b |>
      select(treatment, interval, cmax, auclast) |>
      pivot_longer(c(cmax, auclast), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "published"),
    by = c("treatment", "interval", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (value - published) / published)
stopifnot(nrow(ss) == 8, all(abs(ss$pct_diff) < 20))

# SC Tmax at steady state: the QW substudy median was 70 h (Supplementary
# Table S2) and the Q2W week-12 median 72 h (Table S3), i.e. about 3 days.
tmax_sc <- nca_mean |>
  filter(interval == "Steady state (week 20)", PPTESTCD == "tmax",
         treatment != "8 mg/kg IV Q4W")
knitr::kable(tmax_sc |> select(-n) |> rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Interval" = interval,
                               "Parameter" = PPTESTCD, "Mean simulated (day)" = value))
stopifnot(all(tmax_sc$value > 1.5 & tmax_sc$value < 4.5))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No inter-individual variability or residual error.** The article and its
  supplement report neither the OMEGA nor the SIGMA estimates. The model is
  therefore a typical-value model with body weight as the only source of
  between-subject difference; `propSd` is fixed to 0. Mean and SD values in
  Tables 1B and 2 come from simulations with variability and cannot be
  reproduced exactly; this mostly affects the SC Q2W regimen, whose troughs
  fall near KM.
* **Units of VM.** Table 1A reports VM as 1.9 mg/L/day, a concentration rate.
  The amount eliminated through the Michaelis-Menten pathway is therefore
  `VM * V2 * C / (KM + C)` (8.6 mg/day for a 70-kg patient). This matches the
  coding of the later model from the same group (`Jamois_2025_tocilizumab_ra`,
  `vmax * central / (km + Cc)`).
* **Which parameters scale with weight.** The Results say that "clearances and
  volumes" increase with weight, with one exponent for clearance terms and one
  for volume terms. Both clearances (CL and Q) take the 0.51 exponent and both
  volumes (V2 and V3) take 0.68. VM, KM and ka are not weight-scaled.
* **Weight exponent cross-check.** The Results state that clearance at 140 kg
  is 47% higher than at 70 kg. With an exponent of 0.51 the increase is
  (140/70)^0.51 = 1.42, i.e. 42%; 47% would need an exponent of about 0.56,
  the upper confidence limit. The published point estimate 0.51 is used. The
  40-kg clearance (-25%) and both volume statements (-32% and +61%) agree with
  the printed exponents.
* **Table 1B first-interval SC Q2W values.** These are lower than the SC QW
  first-interval values even though the first dose is the same, so they are
  not used as a check (see the NCA comparison above).
* **SC bioavailability.** Table 1A rounds FSC to 0.80; the Results text gives
  79.5% (95% CI 77.9-81.1%). The more precise 0.795 is used.
* **IV infusion duration.** The paper does not state the infusion duration;
  the labelled 1-hour infusion is assumed.
* **Weight distribution.** The virtual cohort uses a deterministic log-normal
  weight grid matched to the pooled Table S1 mean and SD within 40-150 kg; the
  paper's simulations used the observed weights.
* **Weight as baseline.** The paper does not say whether weight was time
  varying in the model; Table 2 stratifies by baseline weight, and the cohort
  here holds weight constant.
